source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text: Yes, we can set it up that way. [URL_002] will serve as the master website, where visitors can learn about your brand and select a location. If someone chooses a location such as Seattle or Bay Area, they will be directed to that location's separate Wix website to make bookings and process payments. With this arrangement, every location will have its own Wix account, bookings, calendar, reporting, and payment setup, while remaining connected through the main [URL_002] website.

value_updates.location_site_architecture: Each operational location uses a separate Wix website and Wix account.

routing_warnings.description: The shared format and location-specific branding concern reusable design structure rather than whether locations use standalone Wix sites.
The exclusion of booking functionality from the master site concerns the master site's role.
The unlinked button is a routing failure, not evidence that standalone Wix sites are absent.
This repeats the unlinked-button routing failure without changing the standalone-site architecture.
The absence of booking software concerns the location booking system; the missing packages separately concern REQ_LOCATION_PACKAGE_CATALOG.
Installing the booking system on the second website is an implementation claim for location booking behavior.
The complaint that the two websites are identical concerns location-specific visitor identity, not their standalone Wix architecture.
The Seattle and master sites being assigned to the wrong pages or profiles is a domain/profile mapping failure.
The transfer lock blocks correction of the site or domain association and belongs to the mapping Requirement.
The client's tentative report that the site or domain was switched concerns correcting the domain/profile mapping.
